examples.explanation: The block [1,-1,5,-2] sums to 3 and has length 4, which is the longest achievable.
The block [-1,2] sums to 1 with length 2, beating every other qualifying block.
The block [1,2] sums to 3; the single element [3] also qualifies but is shorter.

hints: Build running prefix sums; a block (j+1..i) sums to k exactly when prefix[i] - prefix[j] == k.
Remember only the first index where each prefix sum appears, since earlier starts give longer blocks.
A single hash map pass computes the best length in linear time.
